title: Slicing Is All You Need: Towards A Universal One-Sided Algorithm for Distributed Matrix Multiplication
problem: Existing distributed matmul algorithms limited to specific partitioning subsets; requires operator redistribution with communication costs
motivation: AI and scientific computing require flexible partitioning strategies; current algorithms fragment support across 1D/2D/1.5D/2.5D variants
method: The algorithm divides matrices into tiles and uses index arithmetic—calculations based on position—to identify which overlapping sections from different tiles must be combined. It runs on graphics processors using a PGAS C++ framework that creates a shared virtual memory space, allowing GPUs on the same machine to send data directly to each other. Because the algorithm calculates overlaps using position-based arithmetic rather than assuming a fixed partitioning pattern, it works with any way of dividing matrices without requiring data to be shuffled around.
key_novelty: Unlike existing algorithms that work only with specific partitioning patterns and require data redistribution, this algorithm uses index arithmetic to support any matrix partitioning scheme directly.
limitations: Limited performance detail; comparison mostly qualitative
